findings.evidence: previous-version digest: jira at dbff837f: 'removed units (351, showing 40)'. All 40 shown items are explained by the current files or by valid rows in docs/audit/recovery/jira/record.md (for example s045, s046 and s050 are restored in commands.md, and s068, s071 and s073 are accepted drops), but 311 items were not shown and could not be checked.
findings.fix: Re-run the removal check with the full digest, for example python3 scripts/audit/audit.py judge-prompt --kind skill --artifact skills/jira/SKILL.md --judge direct --digest-dir <dir>, and add a row to docs/audit/recovery/jira/record.md for any unit no section row covers, or restore it to references/.

findings.evidence: '**Story or task:** creating one or rewriting its description, also read `references/story-anatomy.md` ... For a draft card, the reply opens with ... Sprint: the next future sprint by default ... Do not load story-anatomy.md for bugs, reads, transitions or comments.' One paragraph mixes the load trigger, the draft output format, sprint policy and a negative load rule. This breaks the process pattern that sections 3.1-3.5 set up.
findings.fix: Split the paragraph into a short numbered sub-procedure under section 3 (1. load story-anatomy.md; 2. draft format: three bold lines first, say nothing was created, ask for review; 3. sprint: next future sprint, reason stated, id written in). Keep every rule and keep the 'Do not load' line as the last item.

findings.evidence: 'move PROJ-27 to done after checking its available transitions' and 'update the summary of PROJ-18 after fetching its current details' (line 35). These should-trigger queries contain the skill's own procedure, so any description triggers on them. Negatives such as 'Design a Jira workflow policy in prose without accessing an instance' are also unnaturally phrased.
findings.fix: Rewrite these as natural user prompts, for example 'can you close out PROJ-27, it shipped yesterday' and 'PROJ-18's title is wrong, should say checkout not cart', and phrase the near-miss negatives the way a user would, for example 'what states should our bug workflow have? just brainstorming'.

findings.evidence: 'DC: UNVERIFIED (exists from Jira 8.4 in practice)'. This minimum-version fact for the createmeta issuetypes endpoint on Data Center has no source URL and no instruction to read it live.
findings.fix: Cite the Atlassian Data Center REST documentation page with the date checked, or replace the version claim with an instruction to probe GET /rest/api/2/issue/createmeta/{project}/issuetypes on the instance and fall back to editmeta or the old createmeta when it returns 404.

findings.evidence: 'the markdown claim is SOURCED from Atlassian developer community thread 101278, which reports raw ADF dropped on edit'. The MCP description format, which SKILL.md's deployment table relies on, cites a community thread, not the vendor's official documentation.
findings.fix: Point to an official Atlassian page or the live tool schema for the description format. If none exists, tell the agent to read the createJiraIssue/editJiraIssue schema description in the session and keep the read-back check, and keep the community thread as supporting context.
